messages:
leila: quick Q — we're considering pushing the sidecarless private-endpoint pattern to beta. main ask: what should the operator API look like and what are the obvious rollout risks?
noah: +1 opt-in. high level: how do we bootstrap auth and rotate creds without an always-on agent?
maya: main concern is cert rotation and trust bootstrapping. with no sidecar we need a pull-based handshake or short-lived tokens. otherwise ops on customer side get messy.
sam: agreed. another is egress IP predictability — customers expect stable source IPs for allowlists. sidecarless means we either document NAT constraints or offer a small egress relay.
leila: thinking operator exposes a Connector CRD that owns: webhook URL, allowed CIDR, mode (sidecarless|relay), trust-anchors. example sketch:
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: tenant-acme-connector
spec:
  mode: sidecarless
  bootstrapWebhook: https://hooks.customer.acme/bootstrap
  allowedSourceRanges:
    - 10.0.0.0/24
  trustAnchorRef: secret/tenant-acme-ca
```
noah: nice. what about fallback? if an app can't do the webhook, we need an automatic relay fallback to avoid downtime.
maya: fallback is fine but needs cost controls. we should have a policy that demotes to relay only when customer opts in or during a short automatic window.
sam: telemetry: we need token usage, handshake latency, and TLS failure counters surfaced in Console so SEs can debug.
leila: agreed. also thinking about an onboarding flow: 1) customer creates `Connector` 2) operator shows `bootstrapToken` in Console 3) customer posts token to their bootstrap endpoint 4) control plane validates and marks connector Ready.
noah: how do we handle cert rotation after Ready? long-lived tokens are a liability. maybe short-lived certs minted by the control plane with a rotation webhook to the customer.
maya: rotation webhook is ok but requires customers to accept inbound HTTPS calls. many customers are behind strict firewalls. alternative: we publish an ephemeral cert in a namespaced secret mirrored via the operator, pull model.
sam: for constrained customers we can offer a small 'connector-agent' image they run as a Job once/day to rotate certs. that keeps the sidecarless promise but provides a rotation path.
leila: good idea — document three footguns: webhook-only, pull-job, and relay fallback. each has tradeoffs: complexity, ops, cost.
eng-bot: CI/canary: sidecarless-e2e stress test (beta) — 2 failures (handshake timeout) on run #472. https://ci.redwood/inv/472
noah: that failure smells like bootstrap webhook timeouts. we should bump retry/backoff and add explicit timeout metrics.
maya: also add a health-check probe for connectors: `connector.status.lastSeen` and `connector.status.handshakeErrors`.
sam: small CLI example for SEs: `rctl connector create --mode sidecarless --webhook https://hooks.customer/bootstrap --cidr 10.0.0.0/24`
leila: plan for rollout: 1) docs + clear opt-in flags 2) alpha to a set of internal customers 3) canary with selective cohorts (small customers first) 4) monitor metrics for 2 weeks 5) expose operator v1.0.
noah: one more: update the Console UI to show fallback mode and cost estimate for relay. SEs will ask customers when relay kicks in.
maya: follow-ups: - write RFC follow-up summarizing handshake modes - add e2e test for rejected bootstrap (400/403) - add metrics and Console tiles
sam: i'll draft the operator CRD docs and CLI help.
leila: thanks team. i'll file the RFC follow-up and tag owners. @sam @maya assignable? :thumbsup:
